🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this update. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ vite (5.4.14 → 5.4.19) · [Repo](https://github.com/vitejs/vite) · [Changelog](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/packages/vite/CHANGELOG.md)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Vite's server.fs.deny bypassed with /. for files under project root

Summary

The contents of files in the project root that are denied by a file matching pattern can be returned to the browser.

Impact

Only apps explicitly exposing the Vite dev server to the network (using --host or server.host config option) are affected.
Only files that are under project root and are denied by a file matching pattern can be bypassed.

  • Examples of file matching patterns: .env, .env.*, *.{crt,pem}, **/.env
  • Examples of other patterns: **/.git/**, .git/**, .git/**/*

Details

server.fs.deny can contain patterns matching against files (by default it includes .env, .env.*, *.{crt,pem} as such patterns).
These patterns were able to bypass for files under root by using a combination of slash and dot (/.).

PoC

npm create vite@latest
cd vite-project/
cat "secret" > .env
npm install
npm run dev
curl --request-target /.env/. http://localhost:5173


🚨 Vite has an `server.fs.deny` bypass with an invalid `request-target`

Summary

The contents of arbitrary files can be returned to the browser if the dev server is running on Node or Bun.

Impact

Only apps with the following conditions are affected.

  • explicitly exposing the Vite dev server to the network (using --host or server.host config option)
  • running the Vite dev server on runtimes that are not Deno (e.g. Node, Bun)

Details

HTTP 1.1 spec (RFC 9112) does not allow # in request-target. Although an attacker can send such a request. For those requests with an invalid request-line (it includes request-target), the spec recommends to reject them with 400 or 301. The same can be said for HTTP 2 (ref1, ref2, ref3).

On Node and Bun, those requests are not rejected internally and is passed to the user land. For those requests, the value of http.IncomingMessage.url contains #. Vite assumed req.url won't contain #

author: garry911128
body:
This pull request introduces significant updates to the UML project application, focusing on enhancing backend functionality, integrating frontend interactions, and improving test coverage. Key changes include the addition of new methods for managing UML diagrams and gadgets, integration of backend events with the frontend, and updates to the test suite to ensure robustness.

### Backend Enhancements:
* **UML Project and Diagram Management:**
  - Introduced methods to manage the current diagram, including `GetCurrentDiagramName`, `InvalidateCanvas`, and `GetCurrentDiagram`. These methods streamline diagram selection and validation processes (`app/backend/umlproject/umlproject.go`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-025870bd6fac35f1b46dbb7ac856525ca8d37dfa3692eb5356331e323d37af51R142-R167) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-025870bd6fac35f1b46dbb7ac856525ca8d37dfa3692eb5356331e323d37af51R178-R192).
  - Added a notification mechanism for draw updates using `RegisterNotifyDrawUpdate` to ensure diagrams emit updates to the frontend (`app/backend/umlproject/umlproject.go`, [app/backend/umlproject/umlproject.goL108-R119](diffhunk://#diff-025870bd6fac35f1b46dbb7ac856525ca8d37dfa3692eb5356331e323d37af51L108-R119)).

* **Gadget and Diagram Type Definitions:**
  - Defined `AllGadgetTypes` and `AllDiagramTypes` to standardize gadget and diagram type management (`app/backend/component/gadget.go`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-09d271970f65f4e23c01143def76dbe31a7bac240324d60ace1bfcf4bc065877R17-R23); `app/backend/umldiagram/umldiagram.go`, [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0f1396c7e9abccb77eaca4464000ff1e8359dba4c2c59b7bf980bd2ee4b6df1aR47-R55).

* **Error Handling and Initialization:**
  - Improved error handling in `InvalidateCanvas` for cases where no diagram is selected or draw data retrieval fails (`app/backend/umlproject/umlproject.go`, [app/backend/umlproject/umlproject.goR142-R167](diffhunk://#diff-025870bd6fac35f1b46dbb7ac856525ca8d37dfa3692eb5356331e323d37af51R142-R167)).
  - Enhanced diagram initialization by registering parent draw updates during diagram creation (`app/backend/umldiagram/umldiagram.go`, [app/backend/umldiagram/umldiagram.goL49-R93](diffhunk://#diff-0f1396c7e9abccb77eaca4464000ff1e8359dba4c2c59b7bf980bd2ee4b6df1aL49-R93)).

### Frontend Integration:
* **Backend Communication:**
  - Added methods to interact with the backend, such as `GetCurrentDiagramName` and `AddGadget`, enabling dynamic diagram updates and gadget creation directly from the frontend (`app/frontend/src/App.tsx`, [app/frontend/src/App.tsxL1-R160](diffhunk://#diff-8a6b4b402514568fbfdc039305ef0b92c85a279c7e8ad92a63cd3f275459ffa3L1-R160)).
  - Implemented event listeners using `EventsOnce` and `EventsOff` to handle backend events and update the frontend graph with new gadgets (`app/frontend/src/App.tsx`, [app/frontend/src/App.tsxL1-R160](diffhunk://#diff-8a6b4b402514568fbfdc039305ef0b92c85a279c7e8ad92a63cd3f275459ffa3L1-R160)).

* **UI Updates:**
  - Introduced new UI components, such as a top menu and buttons for fetching the current diagram name and adding gadgets, improving user interaction with the application (`app/frontend/src/App.tsx`, [app/frontend/src/App.tsxL1-R160](diffhunk://#diff-8a6b4b402514568fbfdc039305ef0b92c85a279c7e8ad92a63cd3f275459ffa3L1-R160)).

### Testing Improvements:
* **New Test Cases:**
  - Added tests for `InvalidateCanvas` to validate error scenarios and successful execution (`app/backend/umlproject/umlproject_test.go`, [app/backend/umlproject/umlproject_test.goR386-R443](diffhunk://#diff-dc7331c377b2832c89f10e965afa97ffa9aa9633f3195cbde0510690d8db08a3R386-R443)).

author: avery-dunn
body:
Removes the final usages of org.projectlombokfrom the main library, as per https://github.com/AzureAD/microsoft-authentication-library-for-java/issues/909

This PR makes the following changes:
 - Remove Lombok's `EqualsAndHashCode` annotation
   - New `equals` and `hashCode` methods were added based on the methods generated by Lombok, though refactored for readability
   - Meaningful unit tests would require duplicate classes using the old code, so they were manually tested to confirm the new methods produce the same hashes are the same as the old generated methods
 - Remove final getter and setter annotations and add appropriately named and scoped methods
   - `AuthenticationResult` appears to have more extensive changes than the other classes, however this is just due to extra some refactoring that groups fields and methods together in a more readable way
 - Changes the scope of the lombok dependency to 'test', which means customers will no longer bring nimbus into their projects because of MSAL
 - A couple tests still use lombok, but this will likely be removed as well in a future PR

author: gadenbuie
body:
Fixes #401

Adds `tool_request` and `tool_result` callbacks that can be registered via `Chat$register_callbacks()`. These callbacks are called just before and just after evaluating the tool request and recieve the `ContenToolRequest` or `ContentToolResult` object as their only argument.

This PR also adds `tool_reject()`, a special classed error that can thrown from inside a tool function or from a `tool_request` callback to prevent a tool function from being called. In the first case, it's simply treated as a tool error, but when used in a callback the tool function is never called if the tool is rejected.

## To Do

- [ ] Add `$chat_async(tool_mode=)` to NEWS (also for `$stream_async()`)
- [ ] Add tests around `tool_mode` when used via `chat$chat_async()` and `chat$stream_async()`. (It's tested more directly in tests that exercise `invoke_tools_async()`.)

This PR introduces the **UI layout and components** for the **Spaces pages** in the ManageHub application. These pages will be central to how users interact with coworking spaces, view available spaces, and manage or book them (functionality to be implemented later).

At this stage, the focus is on building a clean, responsive, and modular frontend interface consistent with the overall design system of ManageHub.

- **Spaces Overview Page** – A grid or list displaying all available workspaces
- **Individual Space Card** – Shows image, name, location, description, and status (e.g., available, booked)
- **Topbar Filters** – Basic UI for filtering spaces by type or availability (non-functional for now)
- **Empty State Component** – Displayed when no spaces are available

- Built with **Next.js 14 App Router**
- Styled using **TailwindCSS** with consistent spacing, padding (`p-4` and above), and rounded corners (`rounded-2xl`)

- No dynamic data fetching yet – all components use mock or placeholder content
- Filters and actions are **non-functional** for now
- No API integration — only the static layout and visual components are included

---

- [x] Responsive and consistent UI matching design standards
- [x] Modular component structure (easy to extend in the future)
- [x] Placeholder components included for future dynamic behavior
- [x] Adheres to the design system and TailwindCSS utility-first approach

author: lqd
body:
This PR and stabilization report is joint work with @Kobzol.

#### Use LLD on `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` by default, and stabilize `-Clinker-features=-lld` and `-Clink-self-contained=-linker` 

This PR proposes making LLD the default linker on the `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` target for the artifacts we distribute, and also stabilizing the `-Clinker-features=-lld` and `-Clink-self-contained=-linker` codegen options to make it possible to opt out.

LLD has been used as the default linker on nightly and CI on this target since May 2024 ([PR](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/124129), [blog post](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2024/05/17/enabling-rust-lld-on-linux.html)), and it seems like it is working fine, so we would like to propose stabilizing it.

The main motivation for using LLD instead of the default BFD linker is improving [compilation times](https://perf.rust-lang.org/compare.html?start=b3e117044c7f707293edc040edb93e7ec5f7040a&end=baed03c51a68376c1789cc373581eea0daf89967&stat=instructions%3Au&tab=compile). For example, in the linked benchmark, it makes incremental recompilation of `ripgrep` in `debug` more than twice faster. Another benefit is that Rust compilation becomes more consistent and self-contained, because we will use a known version of the LLD linker, rather than "whatever GNU ld version is on the user's system".

Due to the performance benefit being so huge, many people already opt into using LLD (or other fast linkers, such as mold) using various approaches ([1](https://github.com/search?type=code&q=%2Flinker-flavor%5B%3D+%5Dgnu-lld-cc%2F), [2](https://github.com/search?type=code&q=%2Flinker-features%5B%3D+%5D%5C%2Blld%2F), [3](https://github.com/search?type=code&q=language%3Atoml+%22-fuse-ld%3Dlld%22), [4](https://github.com/search?type=code&q=language%3Arust+%22-fuse-ld%3Dlld%22)). By making LLD the default linker on the `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` target, we will be able to speed up Rust compilation out of the box, without users having to opt in or know about it.

> You can find an extended version of this stabilization report which includes analysis of crater results and more data [here](https://hackmd.io/tFDifkUcSLGoHPBRIl0z8w?view).

## What is being stabilized
- `rust-lld` being used as the default linker on the `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` target.
    - Note that `rust-lld` is being enabled by default in the compiler artifacts distributed by our CI/rustup. It is still possible to use the system linker by default using `rust.lld = false` in `bootstrap.toml`, which can be useful e.g. for some Linux distros that might not want to use the LLD we distribute.
    - This is done by activating the LLD linker feature and using the self-contained linker on that target. Both of which are also usable on the CLI, if some opt outs are necessary, as described below.
- `-Clinker-features=-lld` on the `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` target. This codegen option tells rustc to disable using the LLD linker.
    - Note that other options for this codegen flag (`cc`) remain unstable.
    - Note that only the opt-out is being stabilized, and only for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`: opting in, or using the flag on other targets would still need to pass `-Zunstable-options`.
    - This flag is being stabilized so that users can opt out of LLD on stable, which would it turn also opt out of using the self-contained linker (since it's an LLD).
- `-Clink-self-contained=-linker`. This codegen option tells rustc to use the self-contained linker. It's not particularly useful to turn it on by itself, but when enabled and combined with `-Clinker-features=+lld`, rustc will use the `rust-lld` linker wrapper shipped with the compiler toolchain, instead of some `lld` binary that the linker driver will find in the `PATH`.
    - Note that other options for this codegen flag (other than the previously stable `y/yes/n/no`).
    - Note that only the opt-out is being stabilized, and only for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`: opting in, or using this flag on other targets would still need to pass `-Zunstable-options`.
    - This flag is being stabilized so that users can opt out of using self-contained linking on stable. Doing this would then fall back to using the system `lld`.

To opt out of using LLD, `RUSTFLAGS="-Clinker-features=-lld"` would be used. To opt out of using `rust-lld`, falling back to the LLD installed on the system, `RUSTFLAGS="-Clink-self-contained=-linker"` would be used.

## Tests

When enabling `rust-lld` on nightly, we also switched x64 linux to use it at stage >= 1, meaning that all tests have been running with lld since May 2024, on CI as well as contributors' machines. (Post opt-dist tests also had been using it when running their test subset earlier than that).

There are also a few tests dedicated to the CLI behavior, or ensuring the default linker is indeed the one we expect:

- [link-self-contained-consistency](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1117bc1e6ce049495b0044dfe756afafc817d2d7/tests/ui/linking/link-self-contained-consistency.rs): Checks that `-Clink-self-contained` options are not inconsistent (i.e. that passing both `+linker` and `-linker` is an error).
- [link-self-contained-unstable](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1117bc1e6ce049495b0044dfe756afafc817d2d7/tests/ui/linking/link-self-contained-unstable.rs): Checks that only the `-linker` and `y/yes/n/no` options for `-Clink-self-contained` are stable.
- [linker-features-unstable-cc](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1117bc1e6ce049495b0044dfe756afafc817d2d7/tests/ui/linking/linker-features-unstable-cc.rs): Checks that only the non-lld options of `-Clinker-features` are unstable.
- [linker-features-lld-disallowed](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1117bc1e6ce049495b0044dfe756afafc817d2d7/tests/ui/linking/linker-features-lld-disallowed.rs): Checks that `-Clinker-features=-lld` is only stable on `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`.
- [link-self-contained-linker-disallowed](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1117bc1e6ce049495b0044dfe756afafc817d2d7/tests/ui/linking/link-self-contained-linker-disallowed.rs): Checks that `-Clink-self-contained=-linker` is only stable on `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`.
- [no-gc-encapsulation-symbols](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1117bc1e6ce049495b0044dfe756afafc817d2d7/tests/ui/linking/no-gc-encapsulation-symbols.rs): Checks that that linker encapsulation symbols are not garbage collected by LLD, so that crates like [linkme](https://github.com/dtolnay/linkme) still work.
- [rust-lld](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1117bc1e6ce049495b0044dfe756afafc817d2d7/tests/run-make/rust-lld): Checks that LLD is actually used when enabled with `-Clinker-features=+lld` and `-Clink-self-contained=+linker`.
- [rust-lld-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1117bc1e6ce049495b0044dfe756afafc817d2d7/tests/run-make/rust-lld-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu): Checks that LLD is used by default on `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` when the bootstrap `rust.lld` config option is `true`.
- [rust-lld-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-dist](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1117bc1e6ce049495b0044dfe756afafc817d2d7/tests/run-make/rust-lld-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-dist): Dist test that checks that our distributed `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` archives actually use LLD by default.

## Ecosystem impact
As already stated, LLD has been used as the default linker on x64 Linux on nightly for almost a year, and we haven't seen any blockers to stabilization in that time. There were a handful of issues reported, these are discussed later below.

Furthermore, two crater runs ([November 2023](https://crater-reports.s3.amazonaws.com/pr-117684-2/index.html), [February 2025](https://crater-reports.s3.amazonaws.com/pr-137044-3/index.html)), were performed to test the impact of using LLD as the default linker. A triage of the earlier crater run was previously done [here](https://hackmd.io/OAJxlxc6Te6YUot9ftYSKQ), but all the impor

Here is everything you need to know about this update. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ vite (5.4.8 → 5.4.19) · [Repo](https://github.com/vitejs/vite) · [Changelog](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/packages/vite/CHANGELOG.md)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Vite's server.fs.deny bypassed with /. for files under project root

Summary

The contents of files in the project root that are denied by a file matching pattern can be returned to the browser.

Impact

Only apps explicitly exposing the Vite dev server to the network (using --host or server.host config option) are affected.
Only files that are under project root and are denied by a file matching pattern can be bypassed.

  • Examples of file matching patterns: .env, .env.*, *.{crt,pem}, **/.env
  • Examples of other patterns: **/.git/**, .git/**, .git/**/*

Details

server.fs.deny can contain patterns matching against files (by default it includes .env, .env.*, *.{crt,pem} as such patterns).
These patterns were able to bypass for files under root by using a combination of slash and dot (/.).

PoC

npm create vite@latest
cd vite-project/
cat "secret" > .env
npm install
npm run dev
curl --request-target /.env/. http://localhost:5173


🚨 Vite has an `server.fs.deny` bypass with an invalid `request-target`

Summary

The contents of arbitrary files can be returned to the browser if the dev server is running on Node or Bun.

Impact

Only apps with the following conditions are affected.

  • explicitly exposing the Vite dev server to the network (using --host or server.host config option)
  • running the Vite dev server on runtimes that are not Deno (e.g. Node, Bun)

Details

HTTP 1.1 spec (RFC 9112) does not allow # in request-target. Although an attacker can send such a request. For those requests with an invalid request-line (it includes request-target), the spec recommends to reject them with 400 or 301. The same can be said for HTTP 2 (ref1, ref2, ref3).

On Node and Bun, those requests are not rejected internally and is passed to the user land. For those requests, the value of http.IncomingMessage.url contains #. Vite assumed req.url won't contain #

This pull request introduces functionality to reactivate "banned" jobs and improves error handling and user feedback across the admin interface. It also includes minor refactoring and enhancements for better code readability and maintainability.

### New Functionality
* Added a `reactivateContent` function in `src/app/services/admin.js` to handle unbanning jobs by sending a PATCH request to the server.
* Implemented a `reactivateJobMutation` in `FlaggedJobsTableContainer.jsx` to manage job reactivation, including success and error handling.
* Added a `handleReactivateJob` function in `FlaggedJobsTableContainer.jsx` to trigger the reactivation mutation.
* Updated `FlaggedJobsTablePresentation.jsx` to include a new "Unban Job" option in the dropdown menu for resolved and deleted jobs.

### Error Handling Improvements
* Enhanced error messages in `FlaggedJobsTableContainer.jsx` to display detailed server responses when available. This applies to errors during job deletion, report disapproval, and report updates. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-94aff293a4eada44656fb83d9ee61062c42b5668f6938d017f06a88f44e030ccL52-R53) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-94aff293a4eada44656fb83d9ee61062c42b5668f6938d017f06a88f44e030ccL63-R77) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-94aff293a4eada44656fb83d9ee61062c42b5668f6938d017f06a88f44e030ccL74-R89)

### UI Enhancements
* Added new props (`isDeleted`, `deletedAt`) to `FlaggedJobModal.jsx` to display deletion status and date for jobs. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-00920fb30ac73787103bed052edf082040cb8f3bc947566927728fc6292876b8R22-R23) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-00920fb30ac73787103bed052edf082040cb8f3bc947566927728fc6292876b8R79-R89)
* Updated `FlaggedJobsTablePresentation.jsx` to include additional `data-testid` attributes for better testability and unique identification of UI elements. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4358ec9f039d1cc56c70ab77e86dc2dcf2064dbbd0b3fe96355da003d3b95d22L115-R118) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4358ec9f039d1cc56c70ab77e86dc2dcf2064dbbd0b3fe96355da003d3b95d22R181) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4358ec9f039d1cc56c70ab77e86dc2dcf2064dbbd0b3fe96355da003d3b95d22L190-R194)

### Minor Refactoring
* Standardized the usage of `join(",")` for query parameter construction in `fetchReports` to improve consistency.

body:
#### Trac ticket number
<!-- Replace XXXXX with the corresponding Trac ticket number, or delete the line and write "N/A" if this is a trivial PR. -->

ticket-36385

#### Branch description
Some of the code for filtering `QuerySet` is overly complex which makes it hard to follow:

- Methods that are nearly identical, e.g. `QuerySet._clone()` vs `QuerySet._chain()` and `Query.clone()` vs `Query.chain()`
- Private API like `Queryset.complex_filter()` which exists for a specific case but can be handled using public APIs
- Flags such as `_defer_next_filter` and `_sticky_filter` that affect the next call to `QuerySet.filter()`
- Passing around deconstructed pieces instead of building a `Q()` as early as possible
- Not using the `klass` argument to `Query.chain()`

I had hoped to eliminate `Query.filter_is_sticky` and pass the `used_aliases` to `Query.add_q()`, but I think that's a non-starter as it has to apply after the _next_ clone. (Hard to get my head around it!)

author: barne856
body:
## Overview

This PR refactors our GitHub Actions workflows to improve maintainability, readability, and separation of concerns. The previous workflow structure using `ci.yaml` and `release.yaml` with multiple triggers has been replaced with a modular system of reusable workflows and event-specific entry points.

## Changes

### New Reusable Workflows

1. **`python-build.yaml`** - Handles Python package building, linting, and testing
2. **`get-version.yaml`** - Extracts package version from the codebase
3. **`pypi-publish.yaml`** - Publishes packages to PyPI
4. **`github-release.yaml`** - Creates and tags GitHub releases with assets
5. **`docker-build.yaml`** - Remains as is, already implemented as a reusable workflow

### New Event-Based Entry Points

1. **`pr-checks.yaml`** - Runs on pull requests to verify code quality without publishing
2. **`dev-push.yaml`** - Runs on pushes to dev branch, building and publishing development Docker images
3. **`main-push.yaml`** - Runs on pushes to main branch, performing full release process

### Testing Configuration

- Set `run_tests` input to `false` in all workflows since the project doesn't currently have any tests
- Simply set it to true once tests have been implemented #14 

## How to Test

- Create a PR to trigger the PR checks workflow
- Push to dev branch to verify Docker image building with dev tags
- Push to main branch to verify full release process (PyPI publish + GitHub release + Docker image)

## Additional Notes

- Path filters have been maintained to prevent unnecessary workflow runs
- All existing functionality from previous workflows has been preserved
- Documentation building remains handled by Read the Docs external integration
- **IMPORTANT** - if the version number has not been incremented since the last push to the main branch, the workflow will fail with a message instructing you to increment the version number rather than publishing and overwriting a version.

Closes #27 Closes #30 Closes #10

### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts

#### [GHSA-859w-5945-r5v3](https://redirect.github.com/vitejs/vite/security/advisories/GHSA-859w-5945-r5v3)

### Summary
The contents of files in [the project `root`](https://vite.dev/config/shared-options.html#root) that are denied by a file matching pattern can be returned to the browser.

### Impact

Only apps explicitly exposing the Vite dev server to the network (using --host or [server.host config option](https://vitejs.dev/config/server-options.html#server-host)) are affected.
Only files that are under [project `root`](https://vite.dev/config/shared-options.html#root) and are denied by a file matching pattern can be bypassed.

- Examples of file matching patterns: `.env`, `.env.*`, `*.{crt,pem}`, `**/.env`
- Examples of other patterns: `**/.git/**`, `.git/**`, `.git/**/*`

### Details
[`server.fs.deny`](https://vite.dev/config/server-options.html#server-fs-deny) can contain patterns matching against files (by default it includes `.env`, `.env.*`, `*.{crt,pem}` as such patterns).
These patterns were able to bypass for files under `root` by using a combination of slash and dot (`/.`).

### PoC
```
npm create vite@latest
cd vite-project/
cat "secret" > .env
npm install
npm run dev
curl --request-target /.env/. http://localhost:5173
```

author: rafostar
body:
Add support for configuring Clapper Enhancers. In order to do that, introduce enhancer proxy object that act as intermediary between player and enhancer plugin.

We cannot give direct access to enhancer instances from code, since they are managed (created and destroyed) by player as/when needed. Also due to some interpreted languages not working with multiple threads. Instead, give proxy objects that will store each enhancer configuration to be applied when an enhancer instance is created.

With this, implementations also gain ability to browse available enhancers, see what they support and change their properties.

Enhancers are now also assigned to player, instead of being only global. This allows to configure them separately on a per player instance basis.

Writing configurable enhancers is super easy too, as all plugin has to do is install standard GParamSpec properties to its class with a corresponding gschema file (for global props only) and its done.

author: sometimes-coding
body:
## Add: Torrent Validation Enhancements

### Key Changes
- **BitTorrent v2 Detection**: Uploads using BitTorrent v2 (BEP 52) are now explicitly rejected in API.
- **Piece Size Validation**: Torrents with a piece size exceeding the configured `max_piece_size` (default: 64 MB) are now blocked during upload.

### Motivation
We've encountered issues where users uploaded torrents with very large piece sizes (e.g., 256 MB), which can cause many BitTorrent clients to crash or become unresponsive. This change introduces a configurable safeguard, as most clients support a maximum piece size of 128 MB or less.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Torrents with piece size > `max_piece_size` should be rejected.
- BitTorrent v2 torrents are blocked with a clear error message.

### Configuration
Ensure the following is present in `config/torrent.php`:
```php
'max_piece_size' => 64 * 1024 * 1024, // 64 MB

author: kosi22
body:
# User Identity Smart Contract

## Overview

The `user_identity` smart contract implements a decentralized authentication and identity management system. It allows users to register decentralized identities (DIDs), request verification, and manage user roles with specific permissions. The contract ensures secure and structured identity verification within decentralized applications.

---

## Features

### User Roles:
- **Patient**: Automatically verified, limited permissions.
- **Doctor**: Can access anonymized data.
- **Researcher**: Can access anonymized data.
- **Admin**: Full permissions including verifying other identities and updating permissions.

### Key Functionalities:
- **Identity Registration**: Users can register their decentralized identity (DID) along with role and metadata.
- **Verification Requests**: Users can submit verification requests, which can be reviewed and approved by admins.
- **Role-Based Permissions**: Permissions managed via role definitions for secure access control.
- **Metadata Updates**: Users can update their metadata.
- **Identity Verification**: Admin users can verify other users' identities.

---

## Data Structures

- **User Identities**:
  - DID (Decentralized Identifier)
  - Role
  - Verification Status
  - Metadata
  - Registration Time
  - Last Updated

- **Role Permissions**:
  - Permissions to verify others, update permissions, and access anonymized data.

- **Verification Requests**:
  - Proof documents
  - Requested roles
  - Status
  - Verifier details

---

## Public Functions

- `register-identity`: Register new identities with automatic verification for patients.
- `submit-verification-request`: Allows users to request identity verification.
- `verify-identity`: Admin-only function to approve verification requests.
- `update-metadata`: Update user's metadata.

---

## Read-Only Functions

- `has-permission`: Check if a user has specific permissions.
- `get-identity`: Retrieve details of a specific user identity.
- `get-verification-request`: Check the status of a user's verification request.
- `is-verified`: Verify if a user's identity is confirmed.
- `get-role-permissions`: Retrieve permissions associated with specific roles.

---

## Error Handling

- `err-owner-only`: Access restricted to contract owner.
- `err-unauthorized`: Action attempted by unauthorized user.
- `err-already-registered`: User is already registered.
- `err-not-found`: Requested entity does not exist.
- `err-invalid-role`: Invalid role provided during registration.

---

## Usage

Deploy this smart contract in decentralized platforms where structured, secure user identity management is essential, such as healthcare, decentralized research platforms, or identity-focused decentralized applications.

---

## Author

This smart contract was developed to facilitate secure and decentralized identity management leveraging blockchain technology.

author: jconn
body:
tflm side of cmsis conv sum changes. Due to the interface change these two changes will need to be in lock-step. Interface change was done in order to keep the activation buffer and weight buffers separate, because activation buffer is temporarily allocated and weight buffer is permanently allocated.

There was an inherited bug found in the depthwise and conv impls that was declaring bias as an output tensor in the prepare stage rather than an input tensor. 

The fully connected layer impl seems to want to use the 1x1 conv code for some tensor shapes, I'm still reviewing if that code path is tested in our test suite. 

Adding in testing flow for the two different cmsis compile modes:
 KERNELS_OPTIMIZED_FOR_SPEED and KERNELS_OPTIMIZED_FOR_SIZE

speed optimization is the default (which uses more buffer space for pre-computation), so I think we've been shipping speed optimization so far. 

Performance validation is still needed for this change. Things that need to be tracked for both performance modes are:

-arena size
-execution time

author: joshuaegala
body:
# Contract Fund Distribution

This smart contract enables secure and transparent fund distribution across defined milestones within a project. Contributors can allocate funds to specific milestones, which can then be marked as achieved and funds withdrawn accordingly.

## Features
- **Milestone Management**: Create, manage, and mark milestones as achieved.
- **Fund Contribution**: Allows contributors to fund specific milestones.
- **Transparent Tracking**: Keeps track of individual contributions per milestone.
- **Secure Withdrawal**: Ensures funds can only be withdrawn upon achieving milestones.

## Data Structures

### Milestones
Each milestone is identified by a unique `milestone-id` and contains:
- **Description**: Brief information about the milestone.
- **Target Amount**: Funds required to achieve the milestone.
- **Funds Allocated**: Current funds contributed.
- **Achievement Status**: Indicates whether the milestone has been completed.

### Milestone Funders
Tracks individual contributions to milestones, associating each funder with their contributed amount.

### Total Contract Funds
Maintains the cumulative funds available within the contract.

## Public Functions

### `create-milestone`
Creates a new milestone.
- **Parameters**:
  - `milestone-id`: Unique identifier for the milestone.
  - `description`: Brief description (up to 100 UTF-8 characters).
  - `target-amount`: Funding goal for the milestone.

### `contribute-to-milestone`
Allows users to contribute funds to a specific milestone.
- **Parameters**:
  - `milestone-id`: Identifier of the milestone.
  - `amount`: Amount to contribute.

### `mark-milestone-achieved`
Marks a milestone as achieved once the funding goal is met.
- **Parameters**:
  - `milestone-id`: Identifier of the milestone.

### `withdraw-milestone-funds`
Withdraws funds allocated to a milestone once achieved.
- **Parameters**:
  - `milestone-id`: Identifier of the milestone.
  - `recipient`: Principal to receive the funds.

## Read-Only Functions

### `get-total-contract-funds`
Returns the total funds accumulated in the contract.

## Error Handling
- `ERR-MILESTONE-EXISTS`: Attempt to create an existing milestone.
- `ERR-MILESTONE-NOT-FOUND`: Milestone does not exist.
- `ERR-MILESTONE-ALREADY-ACHIEVED`: Milestone already marked achieved or incorrect status for action.
- `ERR-INSUFFICIENT-FUNDS`: Not enough funds to mark milestone as achieved.
- `ERR-UNAUTHORIZED`: Unauthorized attempt to perform an action.

body:
### Background and Links
* I've seen other people like [asdf developers](https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf/tree/master/scripts) use the `.bash` file suffix; I think that'd be a good way to communicate how the file formerly known as includes.sh has been designed and tested
* I'd also like to clarify upstream (`.biobuddies/includes.bash`) and downstream (something that sources and extends it) shell includes; in the words of Tim Peters, "Namespaces are one honking great idea -- let's do more of those!"
* `cookiecutter`
    - Can handle multiple files
    - Is more likely to be familiar to developers than curl in a pre-commit hook
    - Can be run independently of pre-commit

### Changes and Testing
* Move `includes.sh` to `.biobuddies/includes.bash`
* Make the old `includes.sh` file a backwards compatability wrapper around the new location, that the old `includes-sh` pre-commit hook creates
* Carry a tweaked version of `pre-commit try-repo` that overrides the repository argument to cookiecutter

### Questions and Followup
* User migration from the `includes-sh` hook to the `cookiecutter` hook
* In a little while, start nagging people to source `.biobuddies/includes.bash` directly, and some time later drop `includes.sh`

#113 
I have created another util function in supabase:
```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION get_gen_file (p_study_guide_id UUID)
RETURNS TABLE (
  name TEXT,
  bucket TEXT
)
AS $$
BEGIN
  RETURN QUERY
  SELECT
    so1.name as name,
    so1.bucket_id as bucket
  FROM
    study_guide sg
  LEFT JOIN
    file f1 ON sg.gen_file_id = f1.id
  LEFT JOIN
    storage.objects so1 ON f1.file_id = so1.id
  WHERE
    sg.id = p_study_guide_id;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
```
I also updated RLS for storage.objects for all authenticated user to be able to read (Took me a while to figure out the problem)

author: fennec82
body:
## About The Pull Request
The big leggies sprites use the base path of "/datum/sprite_accessory/tail/taur", which carries with it the taur clip mask. This caused clothing to incorrectly render with the clip mask rather than how they do on bipedal characters. This PR adds an exemption to the big leggies parent type so that clothing renders over the boosted legs (See attachment). 

## Why it's good for the game
Fixes an error that was bugging me and I'm sure a lot of other people who play characters that utilize the big leggies tail type.

## Proof of testing
![Screenshot 2025-04-30 182903](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f9d800c3-7d3a-476d-a222-ccef6fabad03)

I tested this with all big leg styles. Clothing renders properly both in the character creator and in game.

## Changelog

:cl: Arrhythmia_V
fix: Clothing now correctly renders over big leggies 
/:cl:

### Description

Currently, applicants are being incorrectly flagged as "eligible" for programs with service area eligibility enabled if they enter a valid address and then go back and edit it to be an invalid address (specifically an address that has zero matches for address correction). This PR corrects that by making sure the `service_areas` array in the applicant data blob is cleared out if there are no matches found for an address.

- [x] Added the correct label: < feature | enhancement | bug | under-development | dependencies | infrastructure | ignore-for-release | database >

### Instructions for manual testing

1. As an admin, add a program with an address question
2. Toggle "address correction" on for the address question and set an eligibility condition for service area
3. Publish the program
4. As an applicant, apply to the program with an eligible address
5. See eligibility message
6. Edit your address
7. Eligibility message should be gone or, if eligibility is gating, you should see an "ineligible" message

Fixes #10004

author: techouse
body:
👋 Hi there! I’m the author of [qs_dart](https://pub.dev/packages/qs_dart), a Dart port of [qs](https://www.npmjs.com/package/qs) for JavaScript.

I’ve given the `buildUrlString` utility method a thorough overhaul to boost its reliability and maintainability. Below is a summary of the key improvements:


### 🚀 Core Enhancements

- Stricter URL Validation
- Now raises an `ArgumentError` for malformed or non-HTTP(S) URLs
- Relies on Dart’s `Uri.parse` and basic checks - no more ad-hoc string assumptions
- Robust Query Encoding
- Switched to the [qs_dart](https://pub.dev/packages/qs_dart) library for all query-string serialization
- Preserves existing multi-valued parameters and URL fragments


### 🛠️ New Dependencies

- [qs_dart](https://pub.dev/packages/qs_dart) (v1.3.8) – Advanced query-string encoding
- [validators](https://pub.dev/packages/validators) (v3.0.0) – Optional URL format checks


### ✅ Expanded Test Coverage

Added new cases in test/utils/utils_test.dart to validate:
- Parameter edge cases
- `null` / empty maps, empty‐string values, overriding existing keys
- URL integrity
- Preserving fragments, rejecting invalid URLs
- Encoding nuances
- Special characters, reserved symbols (`@`, `/`), spaces vs. plus signs
- Data types & collections
- Numeric and boolean values, lists (including empty items), insertion-order guarantees

These tests ensure that `buildUrlString` behaves correctly across all common and edge scenarios.

author: lucasnewman
body:
This pulls in the mlx-whisper model with some minor tweaks to make it better for our usage:

1) It computes the mel filterbank in code instead of relying on external assets
2) It uses soundfile to load audio instead of ffmpeg from a shell command

This will also avoid the torch dependency from the mlx-whisper repo. I verified the transcription path for reference audio with TTS still works the same way.

Since this is the first STT model, I didn't try to (over-)generalize the model loading and invocation, but it's set up to easily extend to that in the future with a standardized .transcribe() call when we add another model.

# Alaska Airlines Pull Request Update Auro design system component dependencies to their latest versions to unlock theming capability. **Enhancements:** - Upgrade multiple Auro design system components to their latest minor and patch versions **Chores:** - Update design tokens and component package versions Additions: - Added a `check-dependencies.js` script to ensure strict validity checks of the Design Tokens repository, and guarantees that the specified version is always used. ## Design Token Version Control & Documentation Clarity The Design Token repository affects most other repositories, so it's important to indicate which version of the tokens' documentation is reflected on the DocSite. By removing the caret (`^`) from the `package.json`, and using exact versioning, we establish a deliberate update process. This process works in tandem with the `versionChecker.js` file, which compares the installed version of Design Tokens with the latest GitHub release and displays a message to consumers: ![Screenshot 2025-05-02 at 9 15 20 AM](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bbe1c066-8963-45f0-8a1b-a3863567aec5) ### Manual Token Management If any additional tokens are added to the Design Token repository, they must be manually added to the DocSite using `auro-tokenlist`; otherwise, they will not be displayed. This is because design tokens do not bundle their documentation, unlike most Auro components. This further enforces a deliberate update pattern, facilitated by the removal of the caret. ## Loading WebCoreStyleSheets in the `head` To mimic how [WebCoreStyleSheets will publish](https://github.com/AlaskaAirlines/WebCoreStyleSheets/pull/210) `essentials-*.css` files in production, we have removed the relevant files from Sass includes and now load them directly into the `head`: ``` ``` This file is necessary to load the web fonts for each respective theme. Since Auro components will use the new Alaska theme (`essentials-as.css`) as their default, that is the file we load on the DocSite. Eventually, we will add theme-switching functionality to allow the DocSite to be viewed in different themes. ## Checklist: - [x] My update follows the CONTRIBUTING guidelines of this project - [x] I have performed a self-review of my own update **By submitting this Pull Request, I confirm that my contribution is made under the terms of the Apache 2.0 license.** _Pull Requests will be evaluated by their quality of update and whether it is consistent with the goals and values of this project. Any submission is to be considered a conversation between the submitter and the maintainers of this project and may require changes to your submission._ **Thank you for your submission!**

author: boomanaiden154
body:
This patch adds a shuffle_repeat_count parameter to tfrecord/file
datasets. This enables setting the repeat_count to something other
than None. Setting the repeat_count to None means it will repeat
indefinitely making it difficult to know when we have iterated over the
entire dataset. Setting it explicitly allows us to iterate over the
entire dataset a precise number of times when needed.

author: nemacysts
body:
autotune currently does some aggregation for service instances where it takes into account the cpu (and if the cpu allocation changes, that's essentially treated as a new service instance) - this is likely done on purpose, but our current thinking is that this is hurting us more than it's helping us

however, changing the autotune query is a much bigger deal than changing the code that uses the results of that query, so we're thinking of simply taking the max from the results across these cpu aggregations - this is a little wasteful, but better than having values that are too low

from looking at the changes (see below) this generally seems to do the right thing - i think the only slightly "funky" thing here is that with this change we'll be biasing recommendations upwards...but that's probably better than being too low

body:
This PR updates the unit conversion logic for joint state handling. It introduces a new conversion script that applies the desired transformations for dataset processing and removes redundant conversion steps in the TrossenArmDriver to use raw unit values downstream.

* Introduces lerobot/scripts/convert.py to compute modified joint actions and states with conversion and scaling.
* Removes unit conversion in the read() and write() methods of TrossenArmDriver for "Present_Position" and "Goal_Position".
* Updates stats computation to reflect the new conversion handling.
* Enforce backward compatibility check for subversion mismatch.
* Add `trossen_subversion` to dataset collection and creation.
